neighbours.label: the word that introduces the alternative course of action chosen over another ('Or, rent...', 'just buy a new one', 'rather than X, she walked'): switching to the other option, not the same actions without a rejected alternative
fire: You could fly to Rome on Friday. Or, take the night train and save a hotel.
If the old laptop keeps crashing, you might as well buy a new one.
Rather than paying for a taxi, the two students walked across the city.
We can eat at the pub tonight. Or, cook pasta at home with the leftovers.
When a bike tyre is that worn, most riders would simply buy a new tyre.
Instead of renting a car for the week, they cycled between the villages.
The museum is crowded on Sundays. Or, visit on a Monday morning instead.
If the fridge is ten years old, you would probably buy a new fridge.
quiet: You could fly to Rome on Friday and stay in a hotel near the station.
The old laptop keeps crashing, so I sent it to my brother to look at.
After paying for the taxi, the two students had dinner in the city.
We ate at the pub last night and the leftovers are in the fridge.
That bike tyre is badly worn, and the rider noticed it on the hill.
They rented a car for the week and drove between the villages.
The museum is crowded on Sundays, especially in the summer months.
The fridge is ten years old and still keeps the milk cold.
